![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14212968/assets/aa0da0d113d1077b1a394f2f45fe839f8845d1bbe544e2497582df18e079c52a.png)

A drone $D$ is approaching a landing point $L$ on the ground at an angle of $\frac{\pi }{4}$ radians to the horizontal. The drone's shadow $S$ is projected onto the ground vertically below the drone. If the drone is approaching the ground with a speed of $6\,\text{ft}/\text{s},$ what is the speed of the drone's shadow?
question.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14212968/assets/9cb94ea5cab43d48da6b836026d302504d7e63fe1260aa81a2b577436b6b4e98.png)

Let $x$ be the distance between the landing point and the shadow, and let $z$ be the distance between the landing point and the drone, as shown above.

We want to find $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}.$
To do this, let's start by setting up a relation between $x$ and $z.$ Relative to the angle $\theta =\frac{\pi }{4},$ the sides $x$ and $z$ are the adjacent and hypotenuse, respectively. So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =\frac{x}{z} \\ \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} & =\frac{x}{z} \\ x & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}z.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we differentiate both sides of the equation with respect to $t$ using implicit differentiation, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}z) \\ \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}.\end{aligned}
$$

We know that $\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}=-6\,\text{ft}/\text{s}$ (negative because the distance between the landing point and the drone is decreasing). Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\cdot (-6)=-3\sqrt{2}.
$$

Therefore, the speed of the shadow is $3\sqrt{2}\,\text{ft/s}.$
